citations.title: Iberdrola secures 98% support at AGM and re-elects Pedro Azagra as CEO

sentences.text: At the general meeting on 29 May 2026, shareholders ratified Pedro Azagra as chief executive and approved Marina Grossi as a new independent director plus the re-election of Maria Angeles Alcala Diaz, Isabel Garcia Tejerina and Anthony L. Gardner; all 23 proposals passed with 98% average support on a 74% quorum, under Executive Chairman Ignacio S. Galan.
Azagra, who succeeded Armando Martinez Martinez after the latter's resignation effective 24 June 2025, co-hosts results presentations with Galan and Chief Financial Officer Jose Sainz.

sentences.quote: the company reiterated its EUR 43 billion investment plan for the period 2026-2028. With this programme, Iberdrola expects to exceed EUR 6.6 billion in net profit in 2026 and reach EUR 7.6 billion in 2028.
sentences.text: Management reiterated a 43 billion euro investment plan for 2026-2028, targeting net profit above 6.6 billion euros in 2026 and 7.6 billion in 2028, with Galan publicly pressing electrification as Europe's competitiveness priority.

sentences.text: Iberdrola SA is shifting its mix toward regulated infrastructure: its 2025-2028 Strategic Plan commits 58 billion euros, with the focus on Networks in the United States and United Kingdom, including 37 billion euros for networks.
The regulated asset base expanded 12% to 51 billion euros in 2025 and is guided to rise around 40% to about 70 billion euros by 2028.

thesis_pillars.text: Iberdrola SA is shifting its mix toward regulated infrastructure: its 2025-2028 Strategic Plan commits 58 billion euros, with the focus on Networks in the United States and United Kingdom, including 37 billion euros for networks. Some 85% of investment is allocated to countries with stable regulatory frameworks, and roughly 70% of network spending goes to the UK and US at about 9.5% nominal return on equity on new projects. Renewables should exceed 60 GW by 2028, with about 85% of output secured under long-term CfDs and PPAs. Net profit rose 12% to 6.29 billion euros in 2025, with adjusted net profit targeted above 6.6 billion euros in 2026.
